html:
Gnawa music is the spiritual music of the Gnawa, a brotherhood in Morocco descended from West Africans brought north across the Sahara as slaves, many in the time of the Saadi and Alaouite sultans.

It is played on the guembri, a three-stringed bass lute, with heavy iron castanets called qraqeb, and with call-and-response singing. In all-night healing ceremonies, the lila, songs call on saints and spirits, and dancers fall into trance.

From the 1960s jazz and rock musicians played with Gnawa masters. Since 1998 a festival in Essaouira draws hundreds of thousands. UNESCO listed it in 2019. It is a reminder of the trans-Saharan trade in people. See also Sufism.
sum: Gnawa music is the spiritual music of the Gnawa, a brotherhood in Morocco descended from West Africans brought north across the Sahara as slaves, many in the time of the Saadi and Alaouite sultans.
